page: Amazon Web Services c9g.24xlarge is an ARM64-based compute-optimized server powered by the AWS Graviton Gen9 processor family, specifically utilizing the Neoverse-V3 model. It features 96 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, meaning hyperthreading is not utilized. The processor is equipped with 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 96 MB of L3 cache. The system includes 192.0 GB of memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, does not include local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. No GPUs are bundled with this configuration.

In benchmark evaluations, the c9g.24xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, ranking in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression. Single-core performance is moderate, placing in the middle 50% for stress-ng single-core tests. The memory subsystem is highly efficient, with read-only cached small block bandwidth and uncached large block bandwidth both reaching top-tier levels, while large block write bandwidth is strong. The server excels in database operations and key-value store workloads, achieving top-tier results in PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations. It also shows strong capabilities in small-to-medium language model prompt processing and text generation.

Given its high physical core density and ARM64 architecture, the c9g.24xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for parallelized, compute-heavy workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it appropriate for high-throughput web serving, multi-threaded data compression, and distributed database nodes. However, workloads requiring high single-threaded performance or massive per-core memory allocations may experience resource constraints. It is suited for high-concurrency web serving, batch processing, and microservices architectures.
